title: Cohomology of a complex as the kernel of the differential on the cokernel of the previous differential
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and $X^\bullet$ a cochain complex of $\mathcal A$ with cohomology $H^n(X^\bullet)=\operatorname{Ker}(d_X^n)/\operatorname{Im}(d_X^{n-1})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $n\in\mathbf Z$ let $\pi_X^n:X^n\to\operatorname{Coker}(d_X^{n-1})$ be the cokernel and $\bar d_X^n:\operatorname{Coker}(d_X^{n-1})\to X^{n+1}$ the unique morphism with $\bar d_X^n\circ\pi_X^n=d_X^n$. Then the composite $\operatorname{Ker}(d_X^n)\hookrightarrow X^n\xrightarrow{\pi_X^n}\operatorname{Coker}(d_X^{n-1})$ induces a monomorphism $\eta_X^n:H^n(X^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Coker}(d_X^{n-1})$ which is a kernel of $\bar d_X^n$. This is natural: for a morphism of complexes $\varphi:X^\bullet\to Y^\bullet$, with $\bar\varphi^n:\operatorname{Coker}(d_X^{n-1})\to\operatorname{Coker}(d_Y^{n-1})$ the morphism with $\bar\varphi^n\circ\pi_X^n=\pi_Y^n\circ\varphi^n$, one has $\eta_Y^n\circ H^n(\varphi)=\bar\varphi^n\circ\eta_X^n$; hence $H^n(\varphi)$ is an isomorphism if and only if the morphism $\operatorname{Ker}(\bar d_X^n)\to\operatorname{Ker}(\bar d_Y^n)$ induced by $\bar\varphi^n$ is an isomorphism.
